mentions.name: DelayKit
mentions.description: DelayKit is a Node.js scheduling primitive backed by Postgres for app-level, per-event scheduling, such as expiring an abandoned cart after 24 hours or debouncing 50 profile updates into one reindex. Developers schedule events with key-based calls like dk.schedule("expire-cart", { key: cartID, delay: "24h" }); handlers receive the key rather than a payload and fetch fresh state at fire time, so DelayKit is only responsible for the scheduled-reminder part. It positions itself between cron (too broad), throughput-focused job queues with run_at bolted on, and heavyweight workflow engines.
mentions.problem: The Node.js ecosystem lacks a good primitive for app-level, per-event scheduling: cron is too broad and still requires writing polling/scheduler code, job queues optimize for throughput and treat run_at as an afterthought, and workflow engines are overkill for simple 'do this thing later, tied to this user' tasks.
mentions.source_excerpt:
Still a bit rough, but working on https://delaykit.dev.

The Node.js ecosystem doesn't seem to have a good primitive for app-level, per-event scheduling (things like "expire this abandoned cart in 24h" or "debounce 50 profile updates into one reindex"). Cron is too broad and you still have write the polling/scheduler code yourself. Job queues optimize for throughput and usually bolt `run_at` on as an afterthought. Workflow engines are overkill for a simple "do this thing later, tied to this user" and want you to adopt their runtime.

DelayKit aims to be the in-between. It is backed by Postgres and uses keys like `dk.schedule("expire-cart", { key: cartID, delay: "24h" })`.
